data.value: The whole model runs on an NVIDIA graphics card through CUDA and cuBLAS. The fastest option. Requires an RTX 20 / GTX 16 series card or newer, driver {0} or newer and three NVIDIA libraries (about {1}).

data.name: ModelTinyHint
data.value: The fastest; makes the most mistakes. Takes about 300 MB of memory. For weak computers and work on the processor.

data.name: ModelBaseHint
data.value: Very fast, acceptable accuracy. Takes about 400 MB of memory. For older laptops and work on the processor.

data.name: ModelSmallHint
data.value: Fast with good accuracy. Takes about 900 MB of memory. Suits the processor as well as a graphics card with 2 GB or more.

data.name: ModelMediumHint
data.value: Very good accuracy, noticeably slower than small. Takes about 2 GB of memory: needs a graphics card with 4 GB or more; slow on the processor.

data.name: ModelTurboHint
data.value: Accuracy close to large-v3 at several times its speed. Needs a graphics card with 6 GB or more.

data.name: ModelTurboNoTranslateHint
data.value: Fast and accurate, but cannot translate into English: pick another model for translation.

data.name: ModelLargeHint
data.value: The best accuracy, copes with difficult vocabulary. Takes about 4 GB of memory: needs a graphics card with 6 GB or more; very slow on the processor.

data.name: CalibrationWhy
data.value: Echo starts recording only when the sound gets louder than the silence level. That keeps the background out of the recording: a fan, the keyboard, the street. With the level too low Echo records noise; with it too high it cuts off the quiet beginning of a phrase.

data.name: CalibrationHow
data.value: Echo will listen to the room and then to your voice, and put the level between them: stay quiet first, then speak. A countdown shows how many seconds are left.

data.name: CalibrationDoneDetails
data.value: The room: {0}, your voice: {1}. Echo will not record anything quieter than the silence level.

data.name: InputEmptyNote
data.value: Leave it empty to return to the value Echo ships with.

data.name: InputWholeError
data.value: Enter a whole number from {0} to {1}

data.name: InputFractionError
data.value: Enter a number from {0} to {1}, for example 0.2

data.name: AdditionalPromptHint
data.value: Words Echo gets wrong: names, product names, terms. Type them separated by commas, for example: Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Ivanov. The model treats them as already said before your phrase and spells them the same way.

data.name: AdditionalCarryInitialPromptHint
data.value: The model works through a recording in pieces of 30 seconds, and the vocabulary affects only the first piece. Turn it on if you dictate for longer than 30 seconds at a stretch and the words of the vocabulary come out wrong further on. Changes nothing while the vocabulary is empty.

data.name: AdditionalNoContextHint
data.value: The model leans on the text it has already recognized, which keeps words and style consistent. Turn it on if the model starts repeating one and the same phrase; recognition also gets slightly faster.

data.name: AdditionalSingleSegmentHint
data.value: The model returns the text of a recording in one piece instead of in parts split at pauses. No effect on phrases shorter than 30 seconds. In a longer recording the upside is predictability: the model moves in even steps of 30 seconds and never gets stuck in one place. The downside: a word on the border of two steps may be lost.

data.name: AdditionalSuppressBlankHint
data.value: The model has to begin its answer with a word, not with nothing. On: a quiet or very short phrase is not lost. Off: the model may write nothing when it could not make out any speech, so it invents less text where there were no words.

data.name: AdditionalTemperatureHint
data.value: How freely the model picks words, from 0 to 1. At 0 it always takes the most likely words, which is the most accurate. Higher values make the text more varied and raise the risk of invented words. Auto: 0, and higher only when recognition has failed.

data.name: AdditionalThreadsHint
data.value: How many processor threads recognition takes. Matters when the model runs on the processor rather than on the graphics card: more threads are faster, but other programs slow down meanwhile. Auto: no more than four.

data.name: AdditionalSuppressRegexHint
data.value: For those who know regular expressions. The model cannot write the pieces of words that match the pattern as a whole: this is how digits are forbidden, for example, so that numbers come out as words. Not set: nothing is forbidden.

data.name: AdditionalBufferMsHint
data.value: How often the microphone hands sound over to Echo, in milliseconds. A lower value means less delay but slightly more processor load.

data.name: AdditionalNumberOfBuffersHint
data.value: How many buffers are set aside for recording. Raise it to 4 or 5 if the recording stutters or drops out on a slow computer.

data.name: AdditionalMicrophoneLevelOutputHint
data.value: While Echo waits for speech during a recording, it prints the microphone level in its window. Helps to pick the silence level by hand. Shown only with the log detail set to Debug or Verbose.

data.name: AdditionalPlaySoundHint
data.value: A short sound when recording starts and when it stops, so you can hear that Echo is listening.

data.name: AdditionalVolumeHint
data.value: How loud the recording sound is, from 0 to 100 percent.

data.name: AdditionalTranslateCaution
data.value: The large-v3-turbo model cannot translate: pick another model for translation.

data.name: AdditionalLogLevelHint
data.value: How much Echo writes about its work in its window. Debug: everything, from loading the model and the devices to the recognition time and the recognized text. Information: only the start and the end of each recording. Warning and Error: only problems.

data.name: AdditionalSilenceThresholdHint
